title: Hosanna to the Royal Son
description: Hosanna to the Royal Son in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 16, headed “Hosanna to Christ, Matt. 21. 9. Luke 19. 38 40”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Ho-san-na to the roy-al Son Of Da-vid's an-cient line, His na-tures two, his per-son one, Mys-te-rious and di-vine.

lines: His natures two, his person one,
The root of David here we find,
Bless'd he that comes to wretched men
To Christ the Lord be given.
Let mortals ne'er refuse to take
Lest rocks and stones should rise, and break

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
